A long read on the point of the sermon and problems with it today - The Embers of Preaching and the Flames of Piety

the whole point of preaching was to stir up a 'sense of' God's wonder

A lot this. The most compelling preaching I hear is that which targets my whole person, with ethos, pathos, and logos. It's not as helpful if all the preacher's preparation was focused on Logos*. It needs ethos, the authority of coming from Scripture, which a lot of more seeker-sensitive preaching lacks. It needs logos, from careful and precise reasoning through the passage. And, it needs pathos, engagement of the emotions with the soaring majesty of God, the crushing sorrow of Sin, and whatever other emotions resonate from the text.

I've thought a sermon could properly be structured as a story, a play with three acts instead of a lecture with three points. First act, exposition, set the scene with an overview of the week's sermon text. Second act, rising action, give the law hard and we find ourselves unable to solve our problem. Third act, redemption and resolution, Christ is our savior, the Gospel is the climax of the story.

And, somehow, the preacher called to this task every week. That sounds exhausting. The more I think about what my pastor has to do, the more grateful I am for my easy life.

*Yes, I'm proud of this pun.
